title: The spectrum of a finite product of fields is a finite discrete scheme whose points are the spectra of the factors

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00ED (algebra-lemma-spec-product, line 3822: Spec(R_1 x R_2) = Spec(R_1) disjoint union Spec(R_2), by R_1 = R_{e_1}), applied n-1 times; Algebra, Lemma 00EC (algebra-lemma-idempotent-spec, line 3775) and Lemma 00E4 (algebra-lemma-standard-open, line 3207: D(f) = Spec(R_f)); a field has the single prime ideal (0). Used in the proof of Morphisms, Lemma 02GL (morphisms-lemma-etale-over-field), morphisms.tex line 8193 ("U is a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions").

proof.text: For each field L_i, PrimeSpectrum (L_i) is a singleton with ideal zero. By Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.exists_comap_evalRingHom_eq, every prime of the finite product is the comap of a prime in a factor, hence the kernel of that projection. Conversely each such kernel is prime by Ideal.comap_isPrime. Injectivity of PrimeSpectrum.sigmaToPi distinguishes the factor indices and hence their kernels.

Use PrimeSpectrum.sigmaToPiHomeo to identify the product spectrum with the disjoint union of the factor spectra. Each factor spectrum is a singleton. Equiv.sigmaUnique gives an equivalence with Fin n, and Nat.card_congr and Nat.card_fin give cardinality n. The disjoint union of singleton spaces is discrete, and the homeomorphism transfers discreteness. These arguments include n = 0: the empty sum corresponds to the spectrum of the zero ring.

For each projection, use the Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Limits instance instIsOpenImmersionMapOfHomForallEvalRingHom to get an open immersion. Its source has only the zero prime, so its image consists exactly of the projection kernel; the reverse inclusion is witnessed by the zero prime. Choose the actual open range f.opensRange. The canonical inclusion of this open subscheme has the same range as f, so IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq and isoOfRangeEq_hom_fac produce the required isomorphism and its factorization equation.

lean.statement: theorem spec_finite_product_fields (n : ℕ) (L : Fin n → Type u) [∀ i, Field (L i)] : (∀ (p : Ideal (∀ i, L i)), p.IsPrime ↔ ∃ i : Fin n, p = Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L i) ⊥) ∧ (∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j → Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L i) ⊥ ≠ Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L j) ⊥) ∧ Nat.card (PrimeSpectrum (∀ i, L i)) = n ∧ DiscreteTopology (PrimeSpectrum (∀ i, L i)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, IsOpenImmersion (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Pi.evalRingHom L i))) ∧ Set.range (fun x : PrimeSpectrum (L i) ↦ (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Pi.evalRingHom L i))).base x) = {p | p.asIdeal = Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L i) ⊥} ∧ ∃ U : (Spec (.of (∀ i, L i))).Opens, (U : Set (Spec (.of (∀ i, L i)))) = {p | p.asIdeal = Ideal.comap (Pi.evalRingHom L i) ⊥} ∧ ∃ e : Spec (.of (L i)) ≅ U.toScheme, e.hom ≫ U.ι = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Pi.evalRingHom L i)))
